correctness.rationale: A complete forward sweep maps an arbitrary residual by a rank-one operator with exact norm |c|/b sqrt(1+c^2/a^2). Normalizing the two eigenvalues to 1 and kappa and parameterizing the rotation by u=tan^2(theta) yields the displayed Phi_kappa exactly. The derivative polynomial has exactly one positive root for every kappa>1 by Descartes' rule, so the scalar maximum is unique. Tangency with level one eliminates u to the reciprocal degree-six polynomial; its reduction through x=kappa+kappa^{-1} has a unique root above two. Continuity plus the exact kappa=6 witness fixes the safe side of the frontier. The packaged checker independently replays the rational witness and root isolation.

value.rationale: Residual norm is a standard stopping and progress metric for linear solvers, while SPD Gauss-Seidel is classically convergent and decreases the associated quadratic energy. The result gives an exact condition-number boundary separating guaranteed completed-sweep residual decrease from possible residual spikes, already in the smallest nontrivial dimension, and supplies a simple exact counterexample. This exposes a concrete mismatch between objective/energy progress and a commonly monitored solver diagnostic.
